solutions.fullSolution: Model-based: learns P_hat(s'|s,a) and R_hat(s,a), then plans against the learned model. Model-free: learns V*(s) or Q*(s,a) directly, skipping the model. Policy search: learns/estimates the gradient of pi_theta directly, or uses black-box/evolutionary search on theta, without necessarily learning any value function.

criteria.description: Correctly maps Q(s,a) to mu_a and sigma(s,a) to the confidence bound.
Correctly identifies the shared optimism-in-the-face-of-uncertainty principle.

solutions.fullSolution: UCB1 chooses argmax mu_a + beta*sqrt(2 ln n / n_a). Q(s,a) plays the role of mu_a (point estimate), sigma(s,a) plays the role of the confidence bound (large for under-visited pairs, shrinking with visits). Both implement 'optimism in the face of uncertainty': add a bonus proportional to uncertainty so uncertain options get tried, fading naturally as uncertainty resolves; RL-05 just applies the same bandit-derived idea to sequential Q-values.

criteria.description: Correctly explains that under-visited pairs get R_max regardless of true reward.
Correctly explains that planning against this optimistic reward automatically seeks out those pairs.

solutions.fullSolution: State-action pairs visited fewer than m times get R_max reward regardless of true reward. Value/Q-iteration against this optimistic reward computes high value for paths toward under-visited pairs, since reaching them looks like reaching max reward. The resulting policy is automatically driven to explore under-visited regions as a side effect of ordinary reward maximization; once (s,a) becomes known, true estimated reward replaces the optimistic placeholder and optimism fades where no longer needed.
